questions.stem: Which among the following is a subcutaneous fungal agent?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sporothrix schenckii
  • Sporothrix schenckii is a subcutaneous fungal agent. The other three mentioned are systemic mycoses.
  • Sporothrix schenckii can infect humans and is the causative agent of Sporotrichosis, commonly known as "rose handler's disease."
  • The most common route of infection is the introduction of spores to the body through a cut or puncture wound in the skin. Infection commonly occurs in otherwise healthy individuals but is rarely life-threatening and can be treated with antifungals.
  • FIG: Nodules along the line of lymphatic drainage.




Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:686.

questions.answerText: Presence of Duffy blood group antigen is protective for P. vivax
questions.solutionHtml:
Presence of Duffy blood group antigen is protective for P. vivax
  • The absence, not the presence, of the Duffy group antigen, is protective against P. vivax
  • Because the Duffy antigen normally serves as the receptor for Plasmodium vivax.
  • Therefore Duffy – negative phenotypes are resistant to P. Vivax invasion and is most commonly seen in black individuals of Africa.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:735

questions.stemHtml: The following vector is not involved in transmission of this disease:
questions.solutionHtml:
Kyasanur forest disease
  • Kyasanur forest disease (KFD) is a tick-borne viral hemorrhagic fever endemic to South India. The disease is caused by a virus belonging to the family Flaviviridae, which also includes yellow fever and dengue fever, which are transmitted by monkeys.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:558.

questions.stemHtml: A 22 year old college going adult has H/o sexual exposure with commercial sex worker, now presenting with painful genital lesions and lymphadenopathy in right inguinal region. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chancroid
  • Chancroidis a bacterial sexually transmitted disease (STD) caused by infection with Haemophilus ducreyi. 
  • It is characterized by painful necrotizing genital ulcers that may be accompanied by inguinal lymphadenopathy (painful – usually unilateral lymph nodes)
  • Chancroid is caused by the bacterium Haemophilus ducreyi and results in painful, superficial ulcers, often with regional lymphadenopathy. Chancroid occurs in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean, and is an important cofactor of HIV transmission.
  • The genital ulcer from chancroid is painful, tender, and nonindurated.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:775.

questions.stemHtml: Which among the following occupation is a risk factor for this presenting illness?
questions.solutionHtml:
A kennel worker
  • The above image shows cutaneous larva migrans.
  • Being a kennel worker is a risk factor for this job as exposure to animal feces is high.
  • Cutaneous larva migrans is a parasitic skin infection caused by hookworm larvae that usually infest cats, dogs and other animals.
  • Humans can be infected with the larvae by walking barefoot on sandy beaches or contacting moist soft soil that has been contaminated with animal faeces


CDC - Zoonotic Hookworm - Biology https://www.cdc.gov/parasites/zoonotichookworm/biology.html

questions.stem: Transmission assessment survey is carried out for:
questions.solutionHtml:
Filariasis
  • Transmission assessment survey is carried out for filariasis as filariasis elimination needs mass drug administration.
  • The transmission assessment survey (TAS) is used to determine when infections have been reduced below target thresholds and Mass Drug Administration can stop.
  • Once MDA has stopped, TAS is used as a surveillance tool to determine that infection levels are sustained below target thresholds.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:587

questions.stem: Which immunoglobulin is elevated in a case of chronic allergy?
questions.solutionHtml:
IgE
  • IgE levels are elevated in chronic allergy.
  • IgE antibodies are normally found in small amounts in the blood, but higher amounts can be a sign that the body overreacts to allergens. This can lead to an allergic reaction. 
  • IgE levels can also be high when the body is fighting off an infection from a parasite or with some immune system conditions.
  • Allergy (Type I hypersensitivity) is always IgE mediated both in acute and chronic phases.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:146.

questions.stemHtml: A 40 years old male from Himachal Pradesh has presented with verrucous lesions in the skin with following microscopic findings from the tissue biopsy. What is the diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chromoblastomycosis
  • The given clinical history and histopathological image are suggestive of chromoblastomycosis.
  • Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic fungal infection of the skin and the subcutaneous tissue caused by traumatic inoculation of a specific group of dematiaceous fungi (usually Fonsecaea pedrosoi, Phialophora verrucosa, Cladosporium carrionii, or Fonsecaea compacta) through the skin.
  • KOH mount or tissue biopsy and staining of the lesion shows – Irregular, dark brown bodies with septae (yeast like bodies) called Sclerotic bodies.



Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:687.

  • This method is mainly to visualize the acid fast organisms. Organism is seen in pink colour with a blue background.



DPDx - Laboratory Identification of Parasites of Public Health Concern. https://www.cdc.gov/dpdx/cryptosporidiosis/index.html

questions.stem: A 48 year old man, hospitalized for 17 days and on IV antibiotics followed by oral course of drugs for acute febrile illness with neutropenia. He had a history of dysuria while admitted and now complaints of loose stools and abdominal pain. Which antibiotic usage has the highest risk for developing pseudomembranous colitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Amino penicillin
  • Pseudomembranous colitis, also called antibiotic-associated colitis or C. difficile colitis, is inflammation of the colon associated with an overgrowth of the bacterium Clostridium difficile.
  • While almost any antibiotic can cause pseudomembranous colitis, some antibiotics are more commonly linked to pseudomembranous colitis than others, including: 3rd generation’s cephalosporins like Ceftriaxone followed by aminopenicillins, Fluoroquinolones, such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin.


Jawetz, Melnick & Adelberg’s Medical Microbiology 28th edition, Page Number:802.
